subject.title: fix: strip volatile output from exec result hash to fix no-progress detection (#93917)

question: Should repeated executions of the same command with the same nonzero status and structured exit identity count as no progress even when their output text differs semantically?
rationale: The patch is correct and well-proven for the reported runaway loop, but this equivalence rule deliberately trades some recovery sensitivity for stronger circuit-breaker availability protection; tests cannot decide the preferred product boundary.

options.title: Accept stable nonzero identity
options.body: Merge after refreshing the exact head, accepting that output differences do not distinguish repeated nonzero outcomes when status, exit code, signal, timeout, and failure kind match.

options.title: Require a narrower discriminator
options.body: Pause and define additional stable semantic failure classes before merge to reduce false-positive blocking for same-exit-code failures.

recommendation.title: Accept stable nonzero identity
recommendation.body: Merge after refreshing the exact head, accepting that output differences do not distinguish repeated nonzero outcomes when status, exit code, signal, timeout, and failure kind match.

likelyOwner.reason: The configurable detector and much of the exec safety behavior trace to their merged history, making them the strongest available owner for the equivalence boundary.
